correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the full-space stationary-state argument. Writing the state entries as A,B,T,w,z as in RESULT.md, the reset transfers the two lower diagonal entries T to the corresponding upper positions and damps w,z. In the two parity blocks the off-diagonal equations are (r+4ih)w=iJ(A−T) and rz=iJ(B−T); both population balances use 2J Im(w)=2J Im(z)=rT. The proposed entries satisfy these identities and trace one. The two reordered block determinants are J²(r²+4J²+16h²)/(4Q²) and J²(r²+4J²)/(4Q²), hence faithfulness. The adjoint fixed-point dissipation identity then forces commutation with the local reset matrix units and their adjoints, so a fixed point must be I⊗G. Commutation with H requires [X,G]=[Z,G]=0 because J,h>0; this proves full-kernel uniqueness, not merely uniqueness within X-states. The standard spin-flip branches give |z|²−AT<0 and |w|²−BT=J²(16h²−4J²−r²)/(4Q²); equality is PPT/separable. Thus the normalized concurrence and the strictly positive-rate boundary are correct. The r=0 generator is excluded. The bundled checker and VERIFICATION.md were inspected but not executed; validation here is algebraic.
